items.title: Emmanuel Sayles Interview, 1959-01-17
items.q: especially like John Morell that was my idol in Coppin how to play banjo

ctx.x: with Faith Margo. No I mean at that time what tune would be the fastest one you'd play? Well the

fastest tune was Tiger A. If I remember well that was the tune you played the fastest. I heard several people say that. Yeah there was no other tune I know that they played any faster than that see because it was something that people wanted to get excited they wanted to you know and then I found out out of New Orleans especially when I when I was in Pensacola and played those plays like a play like Mobile, Montgomery and I haven't played but played for them it went down further in Florida and they had good bands…
Pensacola band they used to hire us but yeah I was wondering about Cootie did he play open or muted horn then

items.title: Emmanuel Sayles Interview, 1961-01-29
items.q: I used to listen to that banjo player like John Morrell, he was very popular and good.

ctx.x: How would they, how would the banjo play on that? Was it straight 4-4 or what'd you do like?

Well, it was, well, I can learn it then, I mean, I first started out playing straight 4-4, and after a while I used to listen to that banjo player like John Morrell, he was very popular and good. And the other ones, that boy named Pley, a little blackie, Santiago. Santiago. His uncle played a very nice banjo. I remember he was playing at a place called Eli Beans that was running that place then. When I was young, I used to stand on the outside and listen at him, you see. That's how I developed ideas about…
And, uh, that was, uh, most of the numbers you would play, like Tiger, Egg, and Bucket, uh.

items.title: Emmanuel Sayles Interview, 1979-12-05
items.q: One of them, I always met John Marrero

ctx.x: When you were coming up, you know like when you first started playing banjo, your idol was John Marrero. That's right.

One of them, I always met John Marrero, but John Sincero was living up in Chicago, I think, and I used to copy some of his stuff. And I actually copied some of Les Paul, the other guy who used to be with, Benny Goodman, a black fellow, he died. He's all a Christian. He's a great way. You have to do that to keep yourself voices down, you see.
What did you like about Marrero? I mean you took over, I mean you saw him quite a bit, I gather, down here. What about his playing did you like? I've never saw him.
